title: One Song Start
pin_title: ADHD One Song Start: Play a Song and Begin During the First Verse
description: Waiting to feel ready can last all day. Pick one song you like and press play. Your only job is to start the task while the first verse is playing. When the song ends you can stop or keep going. The music gives a soft boundary and makes the beginning feel lighter. Most days you will still be working when the song finishes. #ADHD #Starting #ADHDTips #Focus

title: Two Minute Tidy
pin_title: ADHD Two Minute Tidy: Clear Only What You Can See in Two Minutes
description: A full clean feels impossible. Set a two-minute timer and clear only the items you can reach without walking away. Put them in their homes or a single bin. When the timer ends you stop. The small clear space is a real win you can see. Tomorrow you can do another two minutes if you want. #ADHD #Tidy #ADHDTips #Clutter

title: Name the Next Step
pin_title: ADHD Name the Next Step: Say One Tiny Action Out Loud Before You Start
description: Big tasks freeze the brain. Before you begin, say the very first tiny action out loud: open the notebook, or put the cup in the sink. Naming it makes the start concrete. You do not need the whole plan. One spoken step is enough to move your body. The rest can wait until that step is done. #ADHD #Starting #ADHDTips #Focus

title: Body Double Quiet
pin_title: ADHD Body Double: Sit Near Someone Working So Focus Feels Easier
description: Working alone can make starting hard. Sit in the same room as someone else who is also working, even if you do not talk. Their presence is a gentle anchor. You can use a video call with cameras on and mics off if you are alone at home. Shared quiet focus often feels lighter than solo effort. #ADHD #BodyDouble #ADHDTips #Focus

title: Phone Away
pin_title: ADHD Phone in Another Room: Leave It So Focus Has a Chance
description: The phone on the desk keeps pulling attention. Put it in another room or a drawer while you do one short task. The distance makes checking harder than just continuing. When the task ends you can go get it. Many people find the first ten minutes feel different without the device nearby. #ADHD #Focus #ADHDTips #Distraction

title: One Page Only
pin_title: ADHD One Page Only: Write or Read Just One Page and Stop
description: A whole chapter or list can feel heavy. Promise yourself only one page. Open the book or notebook, finish that single page, and close it. The small finish is still a finish. Often the next page feels easier after the first one is done, but you are allowed to stop. #ADHD #Reading #ADHDTips #Starting

title: Kind Timer Reset
pin_title: ADHD Kind Timer: When the Alarm Rings, Choose Softly What Comes Next
description: Timers can feel like pressure. When yours rings, pause and ask what would feel kind right now: continue, switch, or rest for two minutes. The alarm is information, not a boss. Choosing after it rings keeps you in charge. Soft resets protect energy better than forcing through. #ADHD #Timers #ADHDTips #SelfCare
